newsitem.title: USA: A look at the jurors in O.J. Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: A look at the jurors in O.J. Simpson civil trial.

text.p: The following are thumbnail sketches of the 12 jurors in the O.J. Simpson civil trial:

-- SEAT 1: Juror #199, a postal worker in his 20s. He is Jamaican-born, of mixed Asian and black descent and has a college degree. He said during jury selection he was surprised at the quick verdict in the criminal case but said he had no opinion on Simpson's guilt or innocence.

-- SEAT 2: Juror #341, a white woman who works in a bank and who appears to be in her late 60s. She wrote on her jury questionnaire that, in her opinion, the use of force in a relationship shows that a person is predisposed to violence.

-- SEAT 3: Juror #186, a white man in his early 30s. He believes that some, but not all, police officers are corrupt. "It's wrong to assume all cops are good," he said, "but I don't say all cops are bad, either." The man also said he developed a passing interest in DNA science after watching the movie "Jurassic Park."

-- SEAT 4: Juror #294, a white woman in her 20s who wrote on her questionnaire that Simpson is "secure, athletic and wealthy." She started the trial as an alternate, then replaced a woman juror who was dismissed for commenting on the appearance of a member of the plaintiffs' legal team.

-- SEAT 5, Juror #266, a white woman in her 30s who grew up in the South. She works as a stage manager for a non-profit community theatre. She said she knew a little about DNA -- a cornerstone of the case -- from high school biology classes.

-- SEAT 6, Juror #257, a Hispanic woman in her 30s. She indicated on her jury questionnaire she did not pay much attention to Simpson's criminal trial -- in which he was acquitted of double murder -- and had few opinions about the case. Said the slow-speed Bronco chase five days after the murders was "silly."

-- SEAT 7, An Asian-American man who replaced a black woman named Rosemary Caraway who was removed from the jury by the judge when it was revealed her daughter worked on the staff of the Los Angeles district attorney. SImpson's lawyers argued unsuccessfully for a mistrial, saying Caraway could have prejudiced other members of the panel during 2-1/2 days of deliberations that took place before she was replaced.

-- SEAT 8, Juror #290, a white man in his 40s. A company manager who specialises in arbitration, he said he would "go in with an open mind." Also said he resolves disputes between employees and "I'm a good listener."

-- SEAT 9, Juror #326, a white man in his 50s who believes police are sometimes involved in cover-ups. "Of course they cover up for each other," he said."It's been done before." He also said it was "possible" that evidence in the case had been tampered with and was doubtful about blood found on a gate at Nicole Brown Simpson's home two months after the murders.
-- SEAT 10, Juror #400, a white woman in her 60s who does invoices and pays bills for legal department at place of employment. Daughter was involved in domestic violence with a boyfriend.

-- SEAT 11, Juror #88, a white woman in her 30s. Asked if she would listen to arguments about evidence-planting by police, she said, "I believe anything is possible." Said during questioning that her husband has strong views that Simpson is innocent, but that she wouldn't discuss the case with him.

-- SEAT 12, Juror #227, a white man in his 50s or 60s. He said he first thought Simpson was innocent but later decided he was "probably guilty." The man, who said his father had been a police officer, called interracial marriages "impractical."
